name: Norwegian
variant: Norwegian Bokmål, standard East Norwegian pronunciation
script: Latin with extra letters: æ, ø, å; left to right
basis: NTNU Norwegian on the Web (NoW), chapters 1-5
src: NTNU: Norwegian on the Web, table of contents, chapters 1-5 with themes, grammar and pronunciation
note: The order follows NoW chapters 1-5 (alphabet; pronouns, present, word order, negation, numbers; object pronouns, modal + infinitive, nouns definite and plural, days and time, directions; reflexives, adjectives, colours, ordinals; demonstratives, food and clothes; past tense). The page gives no CEFR label: treating these chapters as A1 is my judgment. Possessives, the separate greetings lesson, moving gender into its own stage and the titles are common course practice. Bokmål with three genders (en, ei, et) is my decision.
hardest: Long vs short vowels and the vowels u, y, ø, æ
Three genders and the definite ending on the noun (bilen, boka, huset)
Verb in second place, and where ikke goes

items: Vowels: long and short, u and y
Consonants: kj-, skj-, rs and silent letters
Introducing yourself: Jeg heter…, Jeg kommer fra…
Pronouns and the present tense in -r: jeg snakker, du bor
Verb in second place: I dag jobber jeg
Questions: hva, hvor, hvem, når, hvordan, and yes/no questions
ikke: negation and where it goes
Numbers and prices: Hva koster det?
Object pronouns: meg, deg, ham, henne
Modal verbs + infinitive: vil, kan, må, skal
Days and telling the time: halv tre, kvart over
Asking for help and directions: til høyre, til venstre, rett fram
en, ei, et: the three genders
Reflexive verbs: jeg setter meg, han vasker seg
Adjectives: en stor bil, et stort hus, store hus
Home, colours and ordinal numbers: første, andre, tredje
Shopping and clothes: denne, dette, disse
Food and drink: Kan jeg få…?
Adjectives after den, det, de: den store bilen
Past tense: jeg snakket, jeg var, jeg hadde
